all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Option B (Classify it as noncurrent solely because management expects renewal) is incorrect because ASC 210-10-45 requires current classification for obligations due within one year unless a qualifying refinancing right exists at the reporting date.

all_distractors.choice_text: Report it as equity because suppliers are involved
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Option D (Report it as equity because suppliers are involved) is incorrect because supplier financing arrangements create a liability, not an equity interest. The identity of the counterparty (supplier) does not affect the balance sheet classificatio

all_distractors.topic: A.002 income statement discontinued operation presentation
all_distractors.choice_text: Combine it with continuing operations until cash is collected
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Option A (Combine it with continuing operations until cash is collected) is incorrect because ASC 205-20 requires separate presentation of discontinued operations once the held-for-sale criteria are met, regardless of whether cash has been collected

all_distractors.topic: A.002 income statement discontinued operation presentation
all_distractors.choice_text: Classify it as extraordinary gain or loss
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Option B (Classify it as extraordinary gain or loss) is incorrect. Under ASC 205 (Income Statement), the correct treatment requires present the component separately as discontinued operations, net of tax, when the criteria are met.

all_distractors.choice_text: Report it only in footnotes because the sale is future-oriented
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Option C (Report it only in footnotes because the sale is future-oriented) is incorrect because ASC 205-20 requires income statement presentation of discontinued operations, not footnote-only disclosure. While the notes contain additional detail abou

all_distractors.topic: A.003 cash flow from operations indirect method
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: This adds back depreciation to net income but omits the gain-removal and AR-increase adjustments.

all_distractors.topic: A.003 cash flow from operations indirect method
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: This adds back depreciation and removes the gain but omits the AR increase adjustment.

all_distractors.topic: A.003 cash flow from operations indirect method
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: This is net income alone, ignoring all cash-flow adjustments.

all_distractors.topic: A.004 statement of changes in equity treasury stock
all_distractors.choice_text: Record treasury stock as an asset held for resale
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Treasury stock is not an asset because a company cannot own its own shares as an asset. Repurchased shares reduce equity and are held in a contra-equity account.

all_distractors.topic: A.004 statement of changes in equity treasury stock
all_distractors.choice_text: Recognize a loss on purchase immediately in income
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Treasury stock transactions are equity transactions, not income transactions. No gain or loss is recognized on the purchase, sale, or retirement of treasury shares.

all_distractors.topic: A.004 statement of changes in equity treasury stock
all_distractors.choice_text: Classify the repurchase as a liability until reissued
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A share repurchase does not create a liability. The company pays cash and reduces equity; there is no obligation to reissue or repay the shares.

all_distractors.choice_text: Defer all revenue until the warranty expires
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The stem states the installation service is distinct from the equipment and separately priced, making it a separate performance obligation under ASC 606. Deferring all revenue until warranty expiration ignores that installation is satisfied at a diff

all_distractors.choice_text: Recognize all revenue when the invoice is issued
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Under ASC 606, revenue is recognized when (or as) each performance obligation is satisfied, not when the invoice is issued. The timing of invoicing is a billing matter that does not determine revenue recognition timing.

all_distractors.choice_text: Recognize revenue only when all cash is collected
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ASC 606 recognizes revenue upon satisfaction of performance obligations, regardless of when cash is collected. Umbra would recognize revenue as the equipment and installation services are provided, even if the customer pays on credit terms.

all_distractors.topic: A.006 contract liability for advance collections
all_distractors.choice_text: Record an equity contribution from customers
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Advance collections from customers are not equity transactions. Under ASC 606, cash received before performance creates a contract liability, not an addition to owners' equity.

all_distractors.topic: A.006 contract liability for advance collections
all_distractors.choice_text: Record all cash received as current-period revenue
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Revenue cannot be recognized before the performance obligation is satisfied. Under ASC 606, unearned amounts are recorded as a contract liability until control transfers to the customer.

all_distractors.topic: A.006 contract liability for advance collections
all_distractors.choice_text: Record a receivable because service will be provided later
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A receivable arises when cash is due but not yet received. Here cash has already been received, so the correct entry is a contract liability (debit cash, credit contract liability), not a receivable.

all_distractors.choice_text: Credit sales revenue for estimated uncollectibles
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Uncollectibles are an expense of extending credit, not a reduction of revenue. GAAP requires recognizing bad debt expense rather than crediting revenue.

all_distractors.choice_text: Wait until a specific customer defaults before recording any expense
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Waiting until a customer defaults is the direct write-off method, which is not GAAP-compliant for material receivables. It violates the matching principle by delaying expense recognition.

all_distractors.choice_text: Report gross receivables with no allowance disclosure
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: GAAP requires the allowance method for material receivables. Reporting gross receivables without an allowance overstates assets and fails to present receivables at net realizable value.

all_distractors.topic: A.008 inventory lower of cost and NRV
all_distractors.choice_text: Ignore declines unless inventory has been sold
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: GAAP requires recognition of inventory declines when they occur, not when the inventory is sold. The lower of cost and NRV test must be applied at each reporting date.

all_distractors.topic: A.008 inventory lower of cost and NRV
all_distractors.choice_text: Use lower of cost or market for all inventory methods without considering method differences
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Under current GAAP, FIFO and average-cost inventory is measured at the lower of cost and NRV (the old LCM rule with a market ceiling/floor no longer applies to these methods).

all_distractors.topic: A.008 inventory lower of cost and NRV
all_distractors.choice_text: Write inventory up to replacement cost when market prices rise
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Inventory write-ups are not permitted under GAAP. The lower of cost and NRV rule only recognizes declines; recoveries are recognized only as reductions of the write-down, not as increases above cost.

all_distractors.choice_text: Assume LIFO liquidation always decreases income
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Option A (Assume LIFO liquidation always decreases income) is incorrect. Under CMA Part 1 accounting principles, the correct treatment requires recognize that older low-cost layers may flow into cost of goods sold and increase current income.

all_distractors.choice_text: Restate prior-year inventory balances to FIFO automatically
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Option B (Restate prior-year inventory balances to FIFO automatically) is incorrect because a LIFO liquidation is an income effect arising from dipping into older cost layers, not an automatic restatement to FIFO. No restatement of prior-year invento

all_distractors.choice_text: Treat the layer liquidation as an investing cash flow
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Option D (Treat the layer liquidation as an investing cash flow) is incorrect because LIFO liquidation affects cost of goods sold, which is an operating item on the income statement. Cash flow classification is not altered by the inventory cost flow

all_distractors.choice_text: Reverse all prior depreciation before testing
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Writing the asset up to fair value is not permitted under U.S. GAAP for long-lived assets held for use. Impairment testing allows recognition of declines but not write-ups above carrying value.

all_distractors.choice_text: Recognize impairment only when management plans to expand use
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Accelerating depreciation changes the pattern of cost allocation but does not address an impairment indicator. Depreciation is a systematic allocation, not an impairment-recovery test.

all_distractors.choice_text: Wait until the asset is sold before considering impairment
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: No action is required only if there is no impairment indicator. A significant adverse change in use is a clear triggering event that requires testing.

all_distractors.choice_text: Disclose only; never accrue litigation losses
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Under ASC 450, a loss contingency that is probable and estimable must be accrued, not merely disclosed. The disclose-only treatment (ASC 450-20-50) applies only when the loss is reasonably possible but not probable.

all_distractors.choice_text: Accrue the maximum possible loss whenever a claim exists
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ASC 450 requires accrual of the best estimate within the range. Accruing the maximum possible loss is appropriate only when no single amount in the range is more likely than any other, in which case the entity accrues the minimum amount and discloses

all_distractors.choice_text: Ignore the matter until the court issues a final judgment
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ASC 450 requires recognition of a probable and estimable loss in the current period's financial statements. Waiting for a final judgment would delay recognition and understate liabilities in the period when the loss became probable.

all_distractors.choice_text: Never adjust financial statements for information received after year-end
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Under ASC 855, Type I subsequent events (conditions that existed at the balance sheet date) require adjustment of the financial statements. The customer's bankruptcy existed at year-end, so adjustment is required — the blanket never-adjust approach i

all_distractors.choice_text: Classify it as a financing event
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The customer's bankruptcy condition existed at year-end, making this a Type I subsequent event per ASC 855. Type I events require adjustment of the financial statements, not just note disclosure. Note-only treatment applies to Type II events (conditi

all_distractors.choice_text: Recognize it only in the next fiscal year because notice came later
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ASC 855 requires adjustment of the current-year financial statements for Type I subsequent events. Deferring recognition to the next fiscal year would misstate the current year's assets (overstated receivables) and the subsequent year's results.

all_distractors.choice_text: Record the leased asset as inventory
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Inventory is held for sale in the ordinary course of business. A leased asset conveys the right to use the underlying asset, not ownership for resale. Under ASC 842, the lessee recognizes a right-of-use asset, not inventory.

all_distractors.choice_text: Recognize no balance sheet amounts for operating leases
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: This was the treatment under the former lease standard (ASC 840), which kept operating leases off the balance sheet. Under ASC 842, virtually all leases — including operating leases that are not short-term — require recognition of a right-of-use asse

all_distractors.choice_text: Record rent only when paid with no liability
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ASC 842 requires the lessee to recognize a right-of-use asset and lease liability at lease commencement. Cash-basis recognition (recording rent only when paid) is not permitted for non-short-term leases under the current standard.

all_distractors.choice_text: Record unrealized gains as treasury stock
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Treasury stock records the cost of shares repurchased by the company, not investment gains. Unrealized gains on debt securities belong in OCI or net income depending on classification.

all_distractors.choice_text: Report all unrealized changes as operating revenue
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Unrealized changes on debt securities are not operating revenue. Depending on classification, they are recognized either in net income (trading) or OCI (available-for-sale) and reclassified upon sale or impairment.

all_distractors.choice_text: Ignore fair value changes until sale under every classification
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Fair value accounting requires recognition of changes in fair value for most debt security classifications. Ignoring changes until sale would violate ASC 320 requirements for available-for-sale and trading securities.

all_distractors.choice_text: Use integrated reporting to replace GAAP financial statements

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Indefinite retention can increase privacy, storage, and legal exposure and does not reflect a governed retention policy.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Data still need controls before dashboard use and after active use, including storage, retention, and disposal.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Immediate deletion may violate retention, audit, legal, or operational requirements.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Moving records without standardizing them preserves the same quality problem in another repository.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Changing credit limits does not cleanse duplicate records and could create additional credit-risk errors.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A calculated field can summarize activity but does not uniquely identify each master record.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A foreign key links to another table, but the vendor master table still needs its own unique primary key.

all_distractors.choice_text: A dashboard filter that hides inactive vendors from standard reports
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A dashboard filter affects presentation and does not provide a unique identifier for database joins.

all_distractors.choice_text: Encryption at rest, because stored customer and invoice records are unreadable without a key
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Encryption protects confidentiality of stored data; it does not by itself require valid relationships between tables.

all_distractors.choice_text: Data visualization, because exceptions are summarized in a dashboard chart
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Visualization can display exceptions but does not enforce valid database relationships.

all_distractors.choice_text: Role-based access, because users receive permissions based on job responsibilities
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Role-based access limits what users can do; it is different from enforcing valid links between invoice and customer tables.

all_distractors.choice_text: An online transaction-processing table used only to enter current sales orders
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: An online transaction-processing table supports current transaction entry, not integrated multi-year analytical reporting across systems.

all_distractors.choice_text: A local spreadsheet maintained independently by each regional manager
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Independent local spreadsheets create version and governance risk and do not provide an integrated reporting architecture.

all_distractors.choice_text: A system log that records failed login attempts for cybersecurity monitoring
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A security log is useful control evidence, but it is not designed to integrate finance data for trend analysis.

all_distractors.choice_text: Review dashboard colors and labels after users begin relying on the report
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Presentation review may improve readability, but it does not verify that source data were completely and accurately extracted, transformed, and loaded.

all_distractors.choice_text: Let analysts manually adjust warehouse totals outside change control when reports appear unusual
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Manual adjustments outside change control can create integrity and audit-trail problems rather than controlling ETL processing.

all_distractors.choice_text: Limit review to whether final reports open successfully in the reporting tool
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A report opening successfully does not prove the underlying source-to-target data are complete or accurate.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A transaction-entry screen supports processing activity; it is not primarily a BI dashboard for monitoring and analysis.

all_distractors.choice_text: An unmanaged spreadsheet with regional definitions that differ from the corporate data dictionary
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Unmanaged spreadsheets with inconsistent definitions undermine dashboard reliability and governance.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A backup log supports recovery evidence, not the dashboard capability of summarizing and analyzing metrics.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A transaction-entry screen would not address misleading chart scaling in an analytical report.

all_distractors.choice_text: The chart needs a larger source data file even if the scale is unchanged
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Adding more data does not correct the misleading effect of a truncated or inconsistent axis.

all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Diagnostic analytics investigates why results occurred; the stem asks for summarizing historical sales by category.

all_distractors.choice_text: Predictive analytics, because it estimates next quarter sales from a model
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Predictive analytics estimates future outcomes; the stem describes reporting last quarter results.

all_distractors.choice_text: Prescriptive analytics, because it recommends the best pricing action
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Prescriptive analytics recommends actions; the dashboard in the stem summarizes historical results.

all_distractors.choice_text: Descriptive analytics, because it reports the decline in contribution margin
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Descriptive analytics would report what happened; the stem focuses on identifying the underlying cause.

all_distractors.choice_text: Predictive analytics, because it forecasts next period contribution margin
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Predictive analytics estimates future outcomes; the stem analyzes causes of a result that already occurred.

all_distractors.choice_text: Prescriptive analytics, because it automatically selects the optimal corrective action
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Prescriptive analytics recommends actions. The stem describes root-cause investigation, not automated action selection.

all_distractors.choice_text: Descriptive analytics, because it summarizes prior-period sales by product
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Descriptive analytics summarizes what happened; the stem asks about estimating next quarter unit sales.

all_distractors.choice_text: Diagnostic analytics, because it explains why a prior variance occurred
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Diagnostic analytics explains why results occurred; the stem describes forecasting future demand.

all_distractors.choice_text: Prescriptive analytics, because it selects the production schedule under constraints
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Prescriptive analytics recommends an action under objectives and constraints. The stem focuses on estimating future sales.

all_distractors.choice_text: Descriptive analytics, because it summarizes current production by department
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Descriptive analytics summarizes what happened; it does not recommend an optimized production mix.

all_distractors.choice_text: Diagnostic analytics, because it explains why last month output missed plan
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Diagnostic analytics investigates causes of past results; the stem asks about recommending a future action.

all_distractors.choice_text: Predictive analytics, because it estimates future demand without recommending an action
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Predictive analytics estimates likely outcomes. The stem goes further by recommending an action under constraints.

all_distractors.choice_text: Clustering observations into groups when no labels are defined in advance
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Clustering groups similar observations without preassigned labels; the stem says the risk categories are already known.

all_distractors.choice_text: Regression, because the model estimates a continuous numeric outcome
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Regression estimates numeric outcomes or relationships, not assignment to known risk categories.

all_distractors.choice_text: Outlier detection, because the model flags unusual records without assigning a class
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Outlier detection flags unusual observations for follow-up; it does not necessarily assign each item to predefined classes.

all_distractors.choice_text: Classification, because each customer is assigned to a predefined approved or rejected category
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Classification uses predefined categories. The stem asks for natural groupings without labels in advance.

all_distractors.choice_text: Regression, because the purpose is to estimate a single dependent variable
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Regression estimates relationships or numeric outcomes, not unsupervised customer segments.

all_distractors.choice_text: Referential integrity, because customer IDs must match records in related tables
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Referential integrity is a database relationship control, not an analytics method for segmenting customers.

all_distractors.choice_text: Classification, because each month is assigned to a predefined risk category
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Classification assigns observations to predefined categories; the stem asks about estimating a cost relationship.

all_distractors.choice_text: Clustering, because it creates groups without a specified dependent variable
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Clustering groups observations based on similarity and does not estimate a specified dependent variable.

all_distractors.choice_text: Outlier detection, because it only flags unusual months for later investigation
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Outlier detection flags unusual observations, but the stem asks for estimating relationships between cost and drivers.

all_distractors.choice_text: Treat each flag as evidence of fraud without further review
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: An outlier is not automatically fraud; it requires follow-up and context.

all_distractors.choice_text: Delete flagged observations before preparing any management report
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Deleting outliers without investigation can remove valid unusual events or conceal errors.

all_distractors.choice_text: Conclude no follow-up is needed when the dashboard total agrees to the general ledger
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Agreement to a total does not explain whether individual unusual payments are valid or require follow-up.

all_distractors.choice_text: Correlation risk, because satisfaction and support usage may move together
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Correlation risk concerns interpreting relationships between variables; the main issue is that the sampled customers may not represent the population.

all_distractors.choice_text: Visualization risk, because survey results can only be shown in tables
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Visualization format is not the main issue. A biased sample can distort conclusions regardless of how results are displayed.

all_distractors.choice_text: Data encryption risk, because survey responses cannot be analyzed securely
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Encryption may protect confidentiality, but it does not address whether the selected customers represent the population.

all_distractors.choice_text: Classification is required whenever two variables move in the same direction
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Classification assigns observations to categories; it is not required simply because two variables move together.

all_distractors.choice_text: The relationship should be accepted as causal if both variables appear on the same dashboard
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Displaying variables on the same dashboard does not establish cause and effect.

all_distractors.choice_text: Clustering proves causation when observations fall into similar groups
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Clustering groups observations by similarity; it does not prove one variable caused another.
