Mandatory access control uses classification labels. The stem describes job-role based access.

all_distractors.choice_text: A programmed validation that checks customer credit limits before processing an order
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Programmed credit limit checks are application controls, not ITGCs.

all_distractors.choice_text: An edit check in the payroll system that prevents duplicate time entries
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Edit checks in payroll are application controls that operate within a specific system.

all_distractors.choice_text: A batch total reconciliation that compares total amounts entered with expected totals
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Batch total reconciliation is an application control for verifying processing accuracy.
Access security controls prevent unauthorized access. The incident involved an unauthorized change.
Application controls operate within applications. The failure is in the change management process.
Computer operations controls cover job scheduling and backup. The incident involves unauthorized changes.

all_distractors.choice_text: Granting new employees full system access by default and removing access only upon termination
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Granting full system access by default violates the principle of least privilege and significantly increases security risk. Access should be granted based on job requirements (need-to-know basis) and removed promptly when no longer needed.

all_distractors.choice_text: Allowing users to share passwords for convenience during busy periods
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Password sharing violates fundamental access security controls and eliminates individual accountability. Each user must have unique credentials; shared passwords create significant vulnerabilities.

all_distractors.choice_text: Using generic administrative accounts for day-to-day operations
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Generic administrative accounts lack individual accountability and cannot be traced to specific users. Each user should have a unique account with appropriate privileges based on their role.
General controls cover the overall IT environment. The stem describes input validation controls.
Output controls verify results after processing. The described controls validate data before entry.
Processing controls verify accuracy during processing. The described controls validate data at entry.
A reasonableness check compares individual values to expected ranges. The stem describes comparing aggregated batch totals to expected totals, not individual reasonableness testing.
A field existence check verifies that required fields contain data. The stem describes batch-to-expected-total comparison, not field validation.
Check digit verification detects data entry errors in identification numbers (such as account numbers) through a calculated digit, not through comparing batch processing totals to expected amounts.
General controls relate to the overall IT environment. The stem describes controls over report output.
Input controls validate data at entry. The stem describes controls over completed output.
Processing controls verify accuracy during processing. The stem addresses output after processing.
A risk management plan is a broader framework for identifying, assessing, and responding to organizational risks. It is not specifically focused on maintaining business operations during disruptions.

A disaster recovery plan (DRP) focuses specifically on recovering IT systems and infrastructure after a disruption. The stem describes maintaining ALL critical business functions (people, processes, facilities), which is the broader scope of a BCP.
A contingency funding plan addresses how an organization will finance operations during a crisis. The stem asks about the plan for operational continuity, not funding arrangements.

all_distractors.choice_text: Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) and Mean Time to Repair (MTTR)
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) is the longest time a process can be unavailable. Mean Time to Repair (MTTR) measures average repair time. The stem specifically describes RTO (4-hour restore) and RPO (15-minute data loss).

all_distractors.choice_text: Business Impact Analysis (BIA) and Risk Assessment (RA)
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Business Impact Analysis (BIA) is the process of identifying critical business functions and assessing disruption impacts. Risk Assessment (RA) identifies threats and vulnerabilities. The stem asks about specific recovery time and data loss metrics,

all_distractors.choice_text: Service Level Agreement (SLA) and Key Performance Indicator (KPI)
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Service Level Agreements (SLAs) are contractual commitments between service providers and customers. KPIs are broad performance measures. The stem describes specific BCP metrics: RTO and RPO.

A mobile site is a portable recovery facility that can be deployed to a location, but it requires setup time and is not typically fully equipped for immediate takeover with real-time data replication.
A warm site has some pre-installed equipment but requires significant configuration and data loading before operations can resume, typically taking hours to days, not minutes.

A cold site provides only physical space and basic infrastructure (power, cooling, raised floors) with no hardware, software, or data. Recovery at a cold site takes days or weeks, not minutes. The stem requires full equipment, real-time replication,
A mirror backup creates an exact copy in real time. The stem describes periodic backups.
A full backup copies all data. The stem describes a strategy mixing daily changes with weekly full backups.
An incremental backup copies data since the last backup of any type. Differential copies since last full backup.

all_distractors.choice_text: The external auditor and the audit committee chair
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The external auditor and audit committee chair do not sign SOX certifications.

all_distractors.choice_text: The internal audit director and the chief accounting officer
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The internal audit director and chief accounting officer do not sign Section 302 certifications.

all_distractors.choice_text: The chief operating officer and the general counsel
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The COO and general counsel are not required to sign Section 302 certifications.

all_distractors.choice_text: The CEO and CFO must certify the financial statements
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: CEO and CFO certification of financial statements is a requirement of SOX Section 302, not Section 404. Section 404 specifically addresses management's assessment of ICFR and the external auditor's attestation.

all_distractors.choice_text: The company must establish a whistleblower hotline
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Establishing a whistleblower hotline is required under SOX Section 301 (audit committee complaint procedures), not Section 404. Section 404 specifically addresses internal control assessment and auditor attestation.

all_distractors.choice_text: The company must rotate its external audit firm every five years
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Mandatory audit firm rotation is not a Section 404 requirement. Section 404 addresses management's ICFR assessment and the external auditor's attestation on that assessment.

all_distractors.choice_text: A maximum of 10 years in prison and $1 million in fines
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The penalties are higher: up to $5 million and 20 years under Section 906.

all_distractors.choice_text: A maximum of 5 years in prison and $500,000 in fines
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The penalties are up to $5 million and 20 years, not $5 million and 10 years.

all_distractors.choice_text: A civil penalty only, with no criminal liability
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Section 906 imposes criminal penalties, not just civil liability.
A minor deficiency is less severe. The described risk level fits a material weakness.
A significant deficiency is less severe than a material weakness. The described risk level is higher.
A control deficiency is the broadest category. The specific severity level fits a material weakness.

all_distractors.choice_text: Reviewing the credit policy documentation only
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Reviewing policy documentation provides evidence of design, not operating effectiveness.

all_distractors.choice_text: Observation of the control being performed once
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Observing the control once provides limited evidence of consistent operation.

all_distractors.choice_text: Inquiry of the credit manager about the control process
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Inquiry alone is the least persuasive form of evidence for testing control effectiveness.
Physical controls protect assets through security measures, not variance analysis.
Segregation of duties separates key functions. The stem describes variance analysis.
Authorization controls involve transaction approval. The stem describes detective review.

all_distractors.choice_text: The IT administrator should not have access to any financial data
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The issue is not that IT administrators should have zero access to financial data, but that combining development, migration, and production access in one person eliminates segregation of duties. IT administrators need appropriate, separated access b

all_distractors.choice_text: Only external consultants should perform system migrations
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: External consultants are not inherently required for system migrations. The core issue is separating incompatible functions (development, migration, production) among different individuals, whether internal or external.

all_distractors.choice_text: All IT staff should have identical system access levels
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Giving all IT staff identical system access levels would worsen the segregation problem, not solve it. Segregation of duties requires separation of functions—access should differ based on role. This option contradicts the principle entirely.

The external auditor's fee structure is not a factor in identifying internal fraud risks. Fraud risk assessment focuses on internal pressures, opportunities, and rationalizations within the organization's processes.

Stock price performance may create pressure on management but is only one potential incentive among many. The most important factor is the complete set of incentives, pressures, and opportunities across ALL processes, not just stock-related pressures

all_distractors.choice_text: The number of employees in the accounting department
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The number of employees in the accounting department is not a direct indicator of fraud risk. Fraud risk depends on the presence of pressure, opportunity, and rationalization, which are independent of department headcount.
The audit committee charter defines the audit committee's role, not internal audit's.
Corporate bylaws govern the overall corporation, not specifically internal audit.
The external audit engagement letter governs the external audit relationship.

all_distractors.choice_text: Evaluating whether the organization's risk management processes are adequate
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Evaluating whether risk management processes are adequate involves objective assessment of evidence and providing an independent opinion — this is an assurance engagement, not a consulting engagement.

all_distractors.choice_text: Auditing the effectiveness of internal controls over cash disbursements
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Auditing the effectiveness of internal controls over cash disbursements is a classic assurance engagement where internal audit evaluates and opines on the adequacy of controls.

all_distractors.choice_text: Assessing compliance with SOX Section 404 requirements
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Assessing compliance with SOX Section 404 requirements involves evaluating and reporting on whether ICFR requirements are met — this is an assurance engagement. A consulting engagement would involve advising on HOW to achieve compliance, not assessin

all_distractors.choice_text: Previous employment as a bank loan officer
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Loan officer experience does not necessarily qualify someone as a financial expert.

all_distractors.choice_text: A graduate degree in finance or accounting
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A graduate degree alone does not qualify without the required practical experience.

all_distractors.choice_text: Membership in a professional accounting organization such as the IMA
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Professional membership is not a criterion for being a financial expert.

all_distractors.choice_text: Conducting surprise audits after discovering irregularities
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Conducting surprise audits is a detective control — it identifies fraud AFTER it has already occurred. The question asks about preventing fraud BEFORE it occurs, which requires preventive controls like a strong control environment.

all_distractors.choice_text: Purchasing fidelity insurance to cover potential losses
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Purchasing fidelity insurance is a risk transfer/corrective measure that addresses financial losses after fraud has occurred. It does not prevent fraud from happening in the first place.

Performing a post-incident forensic investigation occurs after fraud has already been detected. It is a detective/corrective measure, not a preventive control. The question asks about preventing fraud BEFORE it occurs.

all_distractors.choice_text: Strong password policies for all users
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Password policies are important but do not protect data during transmission.

all_distractors.choice_text: Physical access controls to the server room
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Physical access controls protect the server room but not data during network transmission.
Encryption at rest protects stored data, not data in transit.
Program change controls govern system modifications. The stem describes ongoing operations.
Application controls operate within specific applications. The stem describes data center operations.
Access security controls govern user access. The stem describes job scheduling and backup.

all_distractors.choice_text: Ensure that only authorized customers can place orders
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Check digits validate the format and integrity of an account number to detect keying errors. They do not authenticate or verify whether the customer is authorized to place orders; that requires separate authorization controls.

all_distractors.choice_text: Prevent unauthorized access to customer accounts
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Check digits do not prevent unauthorized access to customer accounts. They are an input integrity control that detects data entry mistakes, not an access control mechanism.

all_distractors.choice_text: Encrypt customer account information in the database
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Encryption is a data protection technique that scrambles data to prevent unauthorized reading during storage or transmission. Check digit verification is an input control that detects data entry errors; it does not encrypt or protect data.
Processing controls verify accuracy during processing. The stem describes pre-implementation controls.
Access security controls govern system access. The stem describes development and testing.
Computer operations controls cover ongoing operations. The stem describes pre-implementation controls.

all_distractors.choice_text: Keep the plan confidential from IT staff to prevent security breaches
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Plans should be shared with IT staff who execute recovery. Confidentiality should not prevent access.

all_distractors.choice_text: File the plan with the SEC and never modify it
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: DR plans should be periodically updated as systems and processes evolve.

all_distractors.choice_text: Rely solely on the plan's documentation without testing since testing is too disruptive
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Testing is critical to validate the plan; documentation alone risks failure during actual disaster.
Tax compliance services are allowed with audit committee pre-approval.
Internal control attestation is a required audit service under Section 404.
Reviews of quarterly financial statements are allowed as part of the audit engagement.
Commitment to competence is about hiring and training, not ethical conduct.
Board independence relates to board composition, not management's ethical behavior.
Organizational structure defines reporting lines, not ethical conduct.
Segregation of duties separates functions across individuals. This stem describes verification by a supervisor, not separation of incompatible functions.
Physical controls involve security measures such as locks and access restrictions. The stem describes a verification process, not physical security.
Authorization involves approving transactions beforehand. The stem describes after-the-fact verification by an independent party.

all_distractors.choice_text: A legitimate management decision within the CFO's authority
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Recording unsupported entries to meet earnings targets is not legitimate; it is management override.

all_distractors.choice_text: An acceptable practice as long as the entry reverses in the next period
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: An entry that is intentionally unsupported to manipulate earnings is never an acceptable practice, regardless of whether it reverses in a subsequent period.

all_distractors.choice_text: A control environment strength because management is involved in the closing process
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Bypassing controls for earnings manipulation is a weakness, not a strength.
A vulnerability assessment identifies security weaknesses, not critical business functions.
A risk assessment evaluates threats, not the specific impact of disruptions on critical functions.
Penetration testing evaluates security defenses, not business continuity requirements.
Risk acceptance involves bearing the risk. The stem describes transferring risk through insurance.
Risk avoidance eliminates the activity. The stem describes insuring against potential losses.
Risk reduction mitigates likelihood or impact. The stem describes transferring financial consequences.
Procurement fraud involves manipulating the purchasing process, not financial statements.
Corruption involves bribery or kickbacks. The stem describes financial misrepresentation.
Asset misappropriation involves theft of assets. The stem describes manipulating financial statements.

all_distractors.choice_text: A documented policy and procedure manual for purchasing
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Policy manuals provide evidence of design, not necessarily actual practice.

all_distractors.choice_text: A verbal explanation from the purchasing manager about the approval process
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Verbal explanations are the least reliable form of evidence.

all_distractors.choice_text: A summary of purchasing activities prepared by the accounts payable supervisor for the auditor
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Summaries prepared by company personnel may be biased and are less reliable.

all_distractors.choice_text: Eliminate the need for data encryption
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Classification does not eliminate the need for encryption; it helps determine where encryption is needed.

all_distractors.choice_text: Reduce the cost of data storage
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Classification may increase storage costs; its purpose is security, not cost reduction.
Classification supports compliance but its primary purpose is determining appropriate controls.
Risk Assessment involves identifying risks. Competence commitment is a Control Environment principle.
Monitoring involves evaluating controls. Competence is part of the control environment foundation.

Control Activities are specific policies and procedures. While competence is important across all components, the principle of demonstrating commitment to competence is specifically a Control Environment principle, not part of Control Activities.
Risk capacity is the maximum risk the organization can bear, not what it chooses to pursue.
Risk tolerance is the acceptable variation from risk appetite. The stem defines risk appetite.
Residual risk is the risk remaining after controls, not the amount of risk the organization is willing to accept.

all_distractors.choice_text: Is only a concern if the DBA also prepares financial statements
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The concern exists regardless of whether the DBA prepares financial statements.

all_distractors.choice_text: Is prevented by implementing a firewall
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Firewalls address external threats, not internal segregation of duties issues.

all_distractors.choice_text: Is acceptable because database administrators need full access to perform their jobs
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Full access privileges do not justify combining incompatible duties; segregation of duties applies at all system levels.

all_distractors.choice_text: It eliminates the need for internal audit
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A hotline supports but does not replace internal audit's broader assurance role.

all_distractors.choice_text: It replaces the need for a code of ethics
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A hotline supplements but does not replace a code of ethics.

all_distractors.choice_text: It automatically notifies the SEC of all reports
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The hotline provides internal reporting channels, not automatic SEC notification.
A control deficiency is the broadest classification. The description fits a specific severity level.
Insignificant deficiency is not a standard PCAOB classification.
A material weakness involves a reasonable possibility of material misstatement, which is more severe than the deficiency described in the stem.
A failover test involves switching to backup systems, not discussion-based walkthrough.
A full-scale simulation involves actual activation of systems and personnel relocation.
A parallel test involves running systems side by side, not discussion-based walkthrough.

all_distractors.choice_text: Performing reviews of interim financial statements
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Reviewing interim financial statements is allowed as part of the audit engagement.

all_distractors.choice_text: Preparing corporate tax returns for the audit client
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Tax return preparation is allowed with audit committee pre-approval.

all_distractors.choice_text: Attesting to management's assessment of ICFR
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Attesting to ICFR is a required audit service, not a prohibited non-audit service.

all_distractors.choice_text: Principle 16 â€” The organization selects, develops, and performs ongoing and separate evaluations
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Principle 16 covers selecting and performing evaluations, not communicating deficiencies.

all_distractors.choice_text: Principle 15 â€” The organization communicates with external parties
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Principle 15 addresses external communication, not deficiency reporting.

all_distractors.choice_text: Principle 14 â€” The organization internally communicates information
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Principle 14 covers internal communication of information, not deficiency reporting.
Manual sample selection is less efficient than data analytics for identifying unusual patterns.
Continuous auditing is broader. The specific technique is journal entry testing with data analytics.
External confirmation involves third-party verification, not internal journal entry analysis.
Pre-numbering does not prevent unauthorized access; it creates accountability through sequential tracking for completeness checking.

all_distractors.choice_text: Reduce the cost of printing documents
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Pre-numbered documents are a control measure, not a cost-saving measure.
Pre-numbering does not encrypt data; it establishes a sequence for completeness checking.

all_distractors.choice_text: The external auditor is independent of the company
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Auditor independence is addressed elsewhere in SOX, not in Section 906.

all_distractors.choice_text: The company has established a whistleblower hotline
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Whistleblower hotline requirements are under Section 301, not Section 906.

all_distractors.choice_text: The financial statements comply with GAAP and the CEO and CFO are responsible for internal controls
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Responsibility for internal controls is covered by Section 302, not Section 906.

all_distractors.choice_text: Human judgment in decision-making can be faulty
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Faulty human judgment is one limitation, but other factors also contribute.

all_distractors.choice_text: Internal control costs must not exceed expected benefits
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Cost-benefit constraints are one limitation, but other factors also contribute.

all_distractors.choice_text: Management override of established controls is always possible
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Management override is one limitation, but other factors also contribute.

all_distractors.choice_text: Replacing all legacy systems with cloud-based solutions
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Cloud migration may be IT strategy but is not a primary data governance objective.

all_distractors.choice_text: Reducing the number of employees in the IT department
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Reducing IT headcount is not a data governance objective.

all_distractors.choice_text: Eliminating all data redundancy in the organization
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Eliminating all data redundancy is neither practical nor a primary governance objective.
A data custodian has technical responsibility for data storage, not policy definition.
A database administrator manages database operations, not data policies.
A data owner is a senior leader accountable for data assets at a strategic level. The stem describes operational, day-to-day data management responsibilities.
Transaction data records business events such as sales orders or invoices, not the stable reference data described in the stem.
Operational data encompasses many types of data used in daily operations. Master data is the specific category described.
Metadata describes data about data, such as definitions and schemas, not the core business entities described.
Completeness and accuracy are two issues. Uniqueness is also affected by duplicate records.
Validity and uniqueness are two issues. Completeness is also affected.
Timeliness relates to data being current. The stem describes completeness, accuracy, and uniqueness.
Predictive analytics forecasts what will happen. The dashboard shows what did happen.
Prescriptive analytics recommends actions. The dashboard shows current metrics.
Diagnostic analytics determines why something happened. The dashboard describes what happened, not why it happened.
Predictive forecasts what will happen. The analysis identified root causes of what already happened.
Descriptive summarizes what happened. The analysis went further to determine causes.
Prescriptive recommends actions. The analysis identified causes, not recommendations.
Descriptive summarizes what happened. The model estimates future outcomes.
Diagnostic analytics determines why something happened. The model predicts future events, not explains past causes.
Prescriptive analytics recommends actions. The model estimates likelihood of future events, not recommends what to do.
Predictive forecasts what will happen. The model recommends specific reorder quantities.
Diagnostic determines why. The model suggests optimal decisions.
Descriptive analytics summarizes what happened. The model recommends optimal reorder quantities, not summarizes past outcomes.

all_distractors.choice_text: Using a 3D pie chart with 12 categories to show budget allocation
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Using a 3D pie chart with 12 categories creates an unreadable visual. Pie charts work best with 5 or fewer categories, and 3D effects distort proportions, making accurate comparison impossible. The correct approach is to choose an appropriate chart t

all_distractors.choice_text: Including as much data as possible on a single chart to maximize information density
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: 3D pie charts with many categories are difficult to read and not best practice.

all_distractors.choice_text: Using multiple different color schemes within a single dashboard for visual interest
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Too much data on one chart makes it cluttered and hard to understand.
Clustering groups similar data points. The described technique finds purchase associations between different products, not groups of similar data points.
Classification assigns items to predefined categories. The technique finds relationships between products, not categorical assignments.
Regression predicts a numerical value. The described technique identifies purchase patterns, not numerical predictions.
Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology, not an AI/learning technique.
RPA automates rule-based tasks but does not improve through learning.
Cloud computing provides resources but does not inherently include learning capabilities.
Unsupervised learning finds patterns without labeled data. The stem describes labeled data.
Reinforcement learning learns through rewards/punishments, not labeled historical data.
Natural language processing analyzes text. The stem describes a classification task with labeled data.
RPA automates repetitive rule-based tasks. The described task involves data entry across systems, which is rule-based automation, not AI learning.
ERP is the underlying business system, not the automation technology.
Blockchain is a distributed ledger. The described task is data entry automation.

all_distractors.choice_text: All blockchain transactions are publicly visible to everyone
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Not all blockchain transactions are public; permissioned blockchains restrict visibility.

all_distractors.choice_text: Data stored on a blockchain can be easily modified by any participant
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Data on a blockchain cannot be easily modified; immutability is a key feature that prevents tampering.

all_distractors.choice_text: Blockchain eliminates the need for any internal controls
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Blockchain changes how some controls work but does not eliminate the need for controls.

all_distractors.choice_text: Guaranteeing that all transactions are accurately classified in the general ledger
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Blockchain does not guarantee accurate classification; it records transactions as entered.

all_distractors.choice_text: Eliminating the need for auditors entirely
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Blockchain changes audit procedures but does not eliminate the need for auditors.

all_distractors.choice_text: Replacing GAAP with blockchain-specific accounting standards
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Blockchain does not replace GAAP; it records transactions under existing standards.

all_distractors.choice_text: Cloud systems never experience downtime or security incidents
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Cloud systems can experience downtime and security incidents like on-premise systems.

all_distractors.choice_text: The organization no longer needs any internal controls over its data
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Organizations remain responsible for their data and internal controls in the cloud.

all_distractors.choice_text: The cloud provider automatically ensures full compliance with all accounting standards
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The cloud provider does not automatically ensure compliance with accounting standards; that remains the organization's responsibility.
PaaS provides platforms for application development. The stem describes managing servers.
FaaS provides serverless function execution. The stem describes managing IT infrastructure.
SaaS provides ready-to-use software. The stem describes managing servers and cloud platforms.
Authenticity concerns whether data is genuine. The primary impact is loss of access.
Authenticity verifies that data is genuine and unaltered. Ransomware primarily impacts availability by encrypting files and preventing access, not authenticity.
Integrity concerns data accuracy. While affected, the primary described impact is loss of access.

all_distractors.choice_text: Relying solely on a strong firewall for all security needs
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Relying solely on a firewall contradicts defense in depth's multi-layer approach.

all_distractors.choice_text: Using only antivirus software to protect all systems
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Using only antivirus provides a single layer, not the multi-layer defense in depth concept.

all_distractors.choice_text: Outsourcing all security functions to a managed service provider
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Outsourcing security alone does not create defense in depth; multiple layers are still needed.
Implementation involves deploying the system. The stem describes initial planning.
Maintenance occurs after implementation. The stem describes planning activities.
Testing occurs after development. The stem describes pre-development analysis and planning activities, not testing.

all_distractors.choice_text: Each department maintains its own separate database for maximum flexibility
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Maintaining separate databases is a limitation of legacy systems, not a feature of ERP.

all_distractors.choice_text: The ERP system eliminates the need for any internal controls
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ERP systems do not eliminate the need for internal controls.

all_distractors.choice_text: ERP systems are less expensive than maintaining separate legacy systems
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ERP systems are typically more expensive initially than maintaining legacy systems.

all_distractors.choice_text: ERP implementations have no impact on business processes
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ERP implementations significantly impact business processes; they do not leave processes unchanged.

all_distractors.choice_text: ERP systems automatically configure themselves without any customization
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ERP systems require significant configuration and customization; they do not configure themselves automatically.

all_distractors.choice_text: Segregation of duties controls are automatically configured and never require adjustment
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Segregation of duties must be carefully configured and maintained in ERP systems; it is not automatic.

all_distractors.choice_text: Data to be stored redundantly in every table for faster access
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Relational databases minimize data redundancy through normalization rather than storing data redundantly in every table.

all_distractors.choice_text: Data to be stored in unstructured documents
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Relational databases store structured data in tables, not unstructured documents.

all_distractors.choice_text: Only the database administrator to access any data
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Relational databases support multiple users with varying access levels.

all_distractors.choice_text: The right to prevent the company from using any data analytics tools
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: GDPR does not prevent companies from using data analytics; it regulates how personal data is processed.

all_distractors.choice_text: The right to demand compensation for any use of their data
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: GDPR does not grant compensation for any data use; it provides rights regarding processing.

all_distractors.choice_text: The right to require the company to share their data with all other customers
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: GDPR provides data portability to the data subject, not sharing with all other customers.

all_distractors.choice_text: Request deletion of their personal information held by the business
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The right to delete is one right, but CCPA also grants the right to know and opt-out rights.

all_distractors.choice_text: Opt out of the sale of their personal information to third parties
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: The opt-out right is one right, but CCPA also grants the right to know and delete.

all_distractors.choice_text: Request that a business disclose the categories and specific pieces of personal information collected about them
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: While the right to know what personal information is collected is a CCPA right, this is only one of several rights. 'All of the above' is the most complete answer.
Continuous auditing is performed by internal audit to test controls periodically. The stem describes management's ongoing monitoring, not periodic audit testing.
Compliance monitoring focuses specifically on regulatory adherence. The stem describes broader monitoring of all control exceptions, not just compliance.
Periodic auditing occurs at scheduled intervals. The stem describes continuous, automated monitoring, not periodic manual review.
Monte Carlo simulation models probability distributions for risk assessment. The described technique analyzes actual invoice digit patterns, not simulated probability outcomes.
Regression analysis models relationships between variables. The described technique examines digit frequency distributions to detect anomalies, not variable relationships.
Cluster analysis groups data into clusters to find natural groupings. The described technique compares actual digit frequencies against Benford's Law's expected distribution, not cluster memberships.
While the email could be a delivery vector, the described attack is a social engineering fraud (BEC/CEO fraud), not a malware infection.
Ransomware encrypts files for payment. The described scenario of a fraudulent email request does not involve file encryption or ransom demands.
Denial of service overwhelms systems with traffic. The described scenario targets a user through email, not system availability.

all_distractors.choice_text: Data governance is only about data security, while data management covers everything else
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Data governance is broader than just data security; it encompasses policies, standards, and oversight for all aspects of data management.

all_distractors.choice_text: Data management establishes policies; data governance implements technical solutions
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Data management does not establish policies; data governance sets policies. Data governance provides the framework; data management executes within that framework.

all_distractors.choice_text: Data governance and data management are synonymous terms
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Data governance and data management are distinct concepts. Governance provides oversight and policies; management handles operational implementation.
Completeness checks whether all required data is present. The issue described is about format and abbreviation consistency, not missing data.
Accuracy measures whether data reflects real-world values. The issue is about standard formatting and consistent abbreviations, not whether the values are correct.
Timeliness measures whether data is current and up-to-date. The issue of standard date formats and consistent abbreviations is about consistency, not timeliness.

all_distractors.choice_text: A detailed data table with 500 rows
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A data table with 500 rows is too dense for quick identification of above/below budget divisions. Tables require reading each row rather than providing visual comparison.

all_distractors.choice_text: A word cloud of division names
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A word cloud shows frequency of text terms, which is not useful for comparing quantitative performance against budget targets.
A 3D pie chart with 15 slices is cluttered and hard to read. Pie charts work best with few categories and are poor for comparing performance against targets.
Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology. The described system reads and interprets text, which is a data analytics function, not a blockchain application.
RPA automates rule-based tasks through user interface interaction. The described system analyzes and interprets contract text, which goes beyond simple automation.
Machine learning trains models on data to make predictions. The described system reads and interprets contract text, which is NLP, not general machine learning.
ISO 27001 certification covers information security management but does not provide the detailed control testing and opinion needed for financial reporting reliance.
SOC 2 Type II reports address security, availability, and processing integrity. While relevant for security assessment, SOC 1 is the standard for financial reporting controls.
PCI DSS compliance addresses payment card data security, not the broader set of financial reporting controls at a SaaS provider.
Unit testing is performed by developers to verify individual components. The stem describes users validating business requirements, which is UAT.
Stress testing evaluates system performance under extreme loads. The described validation of business requirements is focused on functionality, not performance under stress.
Integration testing verifies that modules work together. The described scenario involves end users validating that the system meets business requirements.
Plan, Do, Check, Act is the Deming cycle for continuous improvement, not a structured incident response framework.
Identify, Assess, Mitigate, Monitor describes a risk management process, not the specific phases of incident response.
Prevent, Detect, Correct is a general control classification, not the comprehensive NIST incident response lifecycle with its distinct phases.
A transaction database handles real-time operational transactions. The described repository is for BI and reporting, not operational transaction processing.
A flat file is a simple text or CSV file without relational structure. The described solution must support querying across multiple source systems.
A data lake stores raw data in native formats using schema-on-read. The stem describes structured, processed data optimized for query performance, which is a data warehouse.

Time series analysis examines data points collected over time to identify trends. The described goal of understanding the relationship between advertising spend and sales revenue involves multiple independent variables, which is multiple regression,
Benford's Law analysis examines digit frequency distributions for anomaly detection. The described analysis explores relationships between business variables, not digit patterns.
Cluster analysis groups similar data points. The described goal is understanding variable relationships affecting sales, not grouping observations.

all_distractors.choice_text: Artificial intelligence, because bank reconciliation requires judgment and learning
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: AI involves learning and adaptation. Bank reconciliation follows defined rules, making it suitable for structured processing rather than AI requiring judgment.

all_distractors.choice_text: Blockchain, because reconciliation always requires distributed ledger technology
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Blockchain is a distributed ledger, not needed for matching existing bank statements against internal records.

all_distractors.choice_text: Natural language processing, because the process involves reading text
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: NLP is used for understanding and interpreting human language text. The described reconciliation process follows predefined matching rules, which is rule-based RPA, not NLP.

all_distractors.choice_text: Within 24 hours of becoming aware of the breach
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: 24 hours is the notification timeline for some sector-specific regulations but not the GDPR standard of 72 hours.

all_distractors.choice_text: Within 7 business days of becoming aware of the breach
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: 7 business days exceeds the GDPR requirement. The regulation specifies 72 hours, which is approximately 3 calendar days.

all_distractors.choice_text: Within 30 days of becoming aware of the breach
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: 30 days is not a GDPR breach notification timeline. The regulation requires notification within 72 hours, which is much shorter.
Periodic substantive testing occurs at intervals. The described approach is continuous, testing 100% of transactions rather than sampling at intervals.
Continuous auditing is internal audit's ongoing automated testing. The described continuous testing approach is classified as compliance auditing when the rules are based on regulatory requirements.
Continuous monitoring is management's responsibility. The described automated testing is performed by internal audit, not management.

all_distractors.choice_text: All employees should have full access to all ERP modules
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Not all employees should have full access. The ERP system's role-based access architecture eliminates the need for manual SoD by enforcing permissions programmatically.

all_distractors.choice_text: Segregation of duties is no longer relevant in an ERP environment
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Segregation of duties remains critical in an ERP environment. The implementation of an ERP system does not eliminate the need for SoD; rather, it shifts enforcement from manual processes to system-configured role-based access controls that must be ca

all_distractors.choice_text: Automated controls eliminate the need for any monitoring
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Automated controls in ERP systems handle monitoring through system logs and exception reports, making manual monitoring less necessary.
A data custodian manages technical storage and security but does not have business-level accountability for data assets.
A database administrator manages the technical database environment, not the business accountability for data assets.
A data steward manages day-to-day data quality and policy enforcement. Ultimate accountability rests with the data owner.

Data extraction is the process of retrieving data from source systems. The described assessment of data quality through profiling occurs before extraction, not as part of the extraction process itself.
Data encryption protects data confidentiality. The described assessment of null values and duplicates is about data quality, not security.
Data normalization organizes data to minimize redundancy. The described activity is assessing existing data quality, not restructuring it.
Administrative controls are policies, procedures, and training. Firewalls, IDS, and network segmentation are technical (logical) controls implemented through technology.
Corrective controls address issues after detection. The described controls are preventive, not corrective.
Physical controls involve tangible barriers like locks and fences. Firewalls and IDS are logical/technical measures.

all_distractors.choice_text: The model will process transactions too quickly
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Processing transactions too quickly is not a risk; speed is generally a benefit of automated ML classification.

all_distractors.choice_text: The model will automatically fix all data quality issues
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: ML models do not automatically fix data quality issues; they reflect the quality of their training data. This is a misconception, not a risk.

all_distractors.choice_text: Machine learning models never make errors
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Machine learning models can and do make errors, particularly when trained on biased or non-representative data. This is a key risk, not a guarantee of error-free performance.

all_distractors.choice_text: Can only be used for cryptocurrency transactions
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Smart contracts are not limited to cryptocurrency. They can automate any conditional business logic, including purchase-to-pay processes.

all_distractors.choice_text: Are legally binding only when printed and signed in paper form
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Smart contracts are self-executing programs stored on a blockchain with terms written directly into code. They do not need to be printed and signed in paper form to be legally binding; their code-based execution is the core innovation of the technolo

all_distractors.choice_text: Require manual approval for every transaction
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Smart contracts do not require manual approval for every transaction; they execute automatically when coded conditions are satisfied.

all_distractors.choice_text: Only use free cloud services to minimize risk
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Free cloud services typically offer fewer security guarantees and should not be relied upon for business functions.

all_distractors.choice_text: Accept all vendor terms without review since cloud providers are always secure
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Accepting all vendor terms without review is poor vendor risk management. Due diligence including SOC reports and contractual protections is essential.

all_distractors.choice_text: Store all data with a single provider only
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Storing all data with a single provider creates concentration risk. Multi-cloud strategies can reduce vendor lock-in risk.

all_distractors.choice_text: Predictive analytics â€” forecasting future returns
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Predictive analytics forecasts future outcomes. The described analysis is investigating past data to understand current return patterns.

all_distractors.choice_text: Descriptive analytics â€” summarizing return rates
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Descriptive analytics summarizes what happened. The stem describes drilling down to identify root causes, which is diagnostic analytics.

all_distractors.choice_text: Prescriptive analytics â€” recommending actions to reduce returns
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Prescriptive analytics recommends actions. The described analysis explores existing data rather than recommending future actions.
Python is a general-purpose programming language used for data analysis but is not the standard query language for relational databases.
HTML is a markup language for web page structure, not a database query language.
Java is a general-purpose programming language, not a dedicated database query language like SQL.
A data portability request asks for data transfer to another organization. The described request is for a copy of data held, not for transfer.
Consent withdrawal involves revoking permission for data processing. The described request is for accessing a copy of personal data, which is a DSAR, not withdrawing consent.
A right to erasure request asks for data deletion. The described request asks for a copy of data, not its deletion.
Classification assigns data to predefined categories. The stem describes finding natural groups based on purchasing behaviors, which is clustering.
Regression predicts numerical values. The described task involves grouping customers, not predicting a numerical outcome.
Association rule mining finds relationships between items in transactions. The described task is grouping customers, not finding item associations.

all_distractors.choice_text: The project is delivered in a single final release
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Single final release describes the waterfall approach, not the iterative delivery cycle of agile.

all_distractors.choice_text: All requirements are fully defined at the beginning and changes are discouraged
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Defining all requirements up front and discouraging changes describes the waterfall approach. Agile embraces changing requirements and iterative development.

all_distractors.choice_text: Testing occurs only at the end of the project
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Testing only at end describes traditional waterfall. Agile includes testing throughout each iteration.
Data mining discovers patterns in large datasets. The described activity is presenting known insights, not discovering new patterns.

Financial reporting summarizes financial transactions in standard report formats. The described presentation combines narrative context with visualizations to communicate insights, which is data storytelling, not standard financial reporting.
Statistical analysis applies mathematical techniques to data. The described presentation combines existing data with narrative, which is financial reporting.
Phishing is a social engineering technique to obtain sensitive information. The described attack involved file encryption and ransom demand, which is ransomware.
Man-in-the-middle intercepts communications between parties. The described attack uses deceptive email to deliver malware, not communication interception.
Denial of service overwhelms system availability. The described attack targeted data access through encryption, not system availability.

all_distractors.choice_text: Eliminating the need for data security
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: MDM does not eliminate the need for data security; it complements security by establishing consistent data standards and governance.
Automating customer communications is a CRM function, not a primary MDM objective.

all_distractors.choice_text: Replacing all existing databases with a single file server
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Replacing databases with a single file server would reduce capability, not improve data management.

all_distractors.choice_text: Giving each bot full administrative access to all systems
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Full administrative access to all systems violates least privilege and creates significant security risk.

all_distractors.choice_text: Disabling all logging to improve bot performance
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Disabling logging eliminates the ability to detect errors, fraud, or unauthorized bot activities.

all_distractors.choice_text: Allowing individual departments to deploy bots independently without central oversight
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Independent departmental deployment without central oversight creates inconsistent controls and security gaps.

all_distractors.choice_text: The confidence interval represents the model's desired outcome
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: A confidence interval represents the range of uncertainty around a prediction, not a desired outcome.

all_distractors.choice_text: The model's predictions are guarantees of future results
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Model predictions are estimates based on historical patterns and cannot guarantee future results as described.

all_distractors.choice_text: Predictive models eliminate the need for budgeting
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Predictive models support but do not eliminate the need for budgeting and planning processes.

Data warehousing involves centralizing data from multiple sources into a single repository for reporting. The described activity of splitting data into related tables to minimize redundancy is database normalization, not data warehousing.
Data mining discovers patterns in data. The described activity is database design, not pattern discovery.
Data encryption protects data confidentiality. The described activity of splitting tables is about data organization, not security.
Penetration testing is a point-in-time simulated attack to identify exploitable vulnerabilities, not the ongoing process of scanning and patching.
Incident response addresses active security incidents. The described process is proactive vulnerability identification and remediation.
Business continuity planning ensures operations during disruptions. The described activity is security-focused vulnerability management.

all_distractors.choice_text: Generative AI always produces perfectly accurate financial information

Unfavorable variances may be trivially small. Significance depends on exceeding thresholds, not on whether the variance is unfavorable.
Favorable is not always positive in effect. Loose standards can produce favorable variances that mask inefficiency or declining quality.

Favorable variances may hide quality problems or outdated standards. They are not universally beneficial and require management review.

Option A uses only traceable fixed costs, omitting direct costs. Segment margin deducts both direct and traceable costs from revenue.
Option B subtracts only direct costs, ignoring traceable fixed costs. Both must be deducted to arrive at segment margin.
Option C subtracts only traceable fixed costs, ignoring direct costs. Both cost categories are traceable and must be deducted.
Option A treats common fixed costs as relevant. Since common costs are unavoidable and continue regardless of the decision, they are irrelevant.
Option C suggests common costs are deducted from revenue for segment decisions. These costs are not traceable to any segment and should be excluded.
Option D adds common costs to segment margin, which overstates performance. Segment margin excludes common costs because they are not controllable at the segment level.
Option A uses market share as a drop criterion. A segment should be dropped based on whether avoidable costs exceed its contribution margin, not market position.
Option B focuses on segment margin being negative. A segment with negative margin may still contribute to covering unavoidable common costs and should be retained.
Option C relies on total revenue being low. Low revenue alone does not justify dropping; the relationship between contribution margin and avoidable costs matters.
Option B limits the BSC to customer measures only. The balanced scorecard integrates four perspectives, not a single dimension.
Option C restricts the BSC to financial measures only. The BSC was developed precisely because financial measures alone provide an incomplete view of performance.
Option D confines the BSC to internal measures only. The framework also includes external perspectives such as customer satisfaction and financial results.
Option B classifies leading indicators as financial measures. Most financial measures are lagging indicators that reflect past performance, not future drivers.
Option C treats leading indicators as lagging indicators. These are opposite concepts — leading indicators predict future results while lagging indicators confirm past outcomes.
Option D equates leading indicators with outcome measures. Outcome measures are lagging indicators that show results already achieved, not future performance drivers.
Option A conflates lagging indicators with leading indicators. Leading indicators drive future performance; lagging indicators measure results already achieved.
Option B describes input measures rather than lagging indicators. Input measures track resources consumed, not the outcomes that lagging indicators capture.
Option C treats lagging indicators as performance drivers. Performance drivers are leading indicators, not lagging outcome measures.
Option A classifies market share as a financial measure. Market share is a nonfinancial metric that belongs to the customer perspective, not the financial perspective.
Option C places market share in learning and growth. This perspective covers employee skills, systems, and culture, not external market position.
Option D assigns market share to internal processes. Internal process measures track operational efficiency and quality, not customer market acceptance.
Option A places employee turnover in internal processes. Turnover reflects workforce stability and belongs in learning and growth, not operational processes.
Option B classifies turnover as a financial measure. Employee turnover is a nonfinancial human capital metric tracked in the learning and growth perspective.
Option C treats turnover as a customer measure. The customer perspective captures external market metrics like satisfaction and retention, not workforce indicators.

Option B places first-pass yield in learning and growth. This perspective covers employee capabilities and innovation, not production quality outcomes.
Option C treats first-pass yield as a customer measure. First-pass yield is an internal production quality metric, not an external customer-facing indicator.
Option D classifies first-pass yield as a financial measure. While quality affects costs, first-pass yield itself is a nonfinancial operational metric.
Option A suggests a one-size-fits-all BSC. Each organization has a unique strategy; the scorecard must reflect its specific objectives and competitive environment.
Option B limits the BSC to industry averages. Industry benchmarks provide context but do not define an organization's unique strategic priorities.
Option C delegates BSC development to consultants. The scorecard must be driven by internal strategy and leadership, not outsourced to external parties.
Option A places variance analysis in internal business processes. Variance analysis compares financial results to budgets and belongs in the financial perspective.
Option B assigns variance analysis to learning and growth. This perspective tracks human capital and innovation, not budget-to-actual financial comparisons.
Option C treats variance analysis as a customer measure. The customer perspective measures satisfaction and market position, not financial performance tracking.
Option B links customer surveys to internal efficiency. Customer satisfaction surveys capture external perceptions of service quality, not internal operational metrics.
Option C treats satisfaction surveys as financial returns. These surveys produce nonfinancial data about customer experiences, not monetary performance numbers.
Option D associates surveys with employee morale. Employee morale belongs to the learning and growth perspective, not the customer perspective.
Option A applies target costing after production begins. By this stage, most product costs are already committed; the design phase offers the greatest cost-influence opportunity.

all_distractors.choice_text: At the end of product life
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Option B places target costing at end of life. Target costing is a forward-looking tool used to set cost targets before production, not a retrospective analysis.
Option C applies target costing during distribution. Distribution occurs after design and manufacturing; cost targets must be established upstream during product development.
Option A limits value engineering to quality improvement only. Value engineering examines the relationship between all product functions and their associated costs.
Option B reduces value engineering to production time only. The methodology evaluates all functions a product performs against the cost of delivering each function.
Option C focuses on cost reduction alone. Reducing cost without considering the value of product functions can diminish customer-perceived value.
Revenue is a financial outcome, not a cost driver; allocation should be based on a cause-and-effect relationship.

all_distractors.choice_text: The same for all cost pools
all_distractors.explanation_wrong: Different cost pools may require different allocation bases; a single base for all cost pools is not appropriate.
Arbitrary allocation undermines cost accuracy; the allocation base should reflect causal relationships.
An output measure may serve as a cost driver but the definition is broader: any factor causing changes in cost.
Input price affects total cost but is not itself a cost driver; drivers are factors that cause costs to change.
Total cost is the aggregated result, not the driver that causes changes in cost levels.
Number of inspections is an activity-based driver used in ABC, not in traditional volume-based costing.
Number of setups is a batch-level ABC driver, not used in traditional volume-based costing.
Number of orders is an ABC-level driver; traditional costing relies on volume-based measures like direct labor hours.
ABC provides limited benefit with only one product since overhead allocation differences do not affect product cost.
ABC is most advantageous when overhead is significant; minimal overhead reduces the benefit of ABC.
When labor is the only significant cost, traditional costing using labor hours already accurately assigns costs.
A push system produces based on forecasts; a pull system in JIT produces only when customer demand triggers production.
JIT aims to minimize inventory levels through pull production and reduced batch sizes.
JIT uses small batch sizes to reduce waste and inventory, not large batches.
Kanban is a visual production signaling system for JIT, not a quality control tool which is a separate concept.
Budgeting is a financial planning process; Kanban is a JIT visual signal that triggers production or material movement.
Cost allocation assigns costs to products; Kanban signals when and what to produce in a JIT system.
Inventory reduction is a goal of JIT, not the emphasis of TQM which focuses on continuous improvement and customer focus.
Speed is one operational objective but TQM primarily emphasizes quality, continuous improvement, and meeting customer needs.
Cost reduction may result from TQM but is not the primary emphasis; TQM focuses on quality and customer satisfaction.
Planning, execution, review describes a project management cycle, not product lifecycle stages in the market.
Purchase, use, disposal describes the customer's consumption process, not the product's market lifecycle stages.
Design, test, implement describes a development process, not the full product lifecycle of introduction, growth, maturity, and decline.
Cost estimation includes regression and account analysis in addition to the high-low method.
Regression is one technique, but cost estimation also includes high-low and account analysis methods.
Account analysis is one technique, but cost estimation also includes regression and high-low methods.
Account analysis classifies costs as fixed or variable based on managerial judgment; product vs period is a different classification.
Controllability classification is used for performance evaluation; account analysis focuses on fixed versus variable cost behavior.
Direct versus indirect classification is for cost tracing; account analysis focuses on cost behavior patterns.
Managerial judgment is used in account analysis, not in engineering estimates which rely on physical input-output relationships.
Industry averages provide external benchmarks; engineering estimates are derived from analyzing physical production relationships.
Historical data is analyzed using regression and high-low methods; engineering estimates use physical relationships between inputs and outputs.
COGM includes direct materials and applied overhead in addition to direct labor, not only direct labor.
COGM includes direct labor and applied overhead in addition to direct materials, not only direct materials.
COGM includes direct materials and direct labor in addition to applied overhead, not only overhead.
Direct labor and manufacturing overhead are conversion costs, not prime costs which are direct materials and direct labor.
All manufacturing costs is a broader category; prime costs specifically include only direct materials and direct labor.
Direct materials and overhead is incorrect; prime costs consist of direct materials and direct labor.
Direct materials and direct labor are prime costs, not conversion costs which are direct labor and overhead.
Direct materials and overhead is not a standard classification; conversion costs consist of direct labor and manufacturing overhead.
Period costs include selling and administrative expenses; conversion costs are manufacturing costs consisting of direct labor and overhead.
Cost assignment includes both tracing direct costs and allocating indirect costs, not only direct tracing.
Estimating is part of cost prediction, not the definition of cost assignment which encompasses tracing and allocation.
Cost assignment includes tracing direct costs in addition to allocating indirect costs, not only allocation.
The board oversees internal control rather than being directly involved in transactions; principle 2 addresses independence and oversight.
Audit committee service is one aspect of board oversight, but principle 2 is broader, covering independence and oversight of the entire internal control system.
Management handles daily operations; the board provides independent oversight of internal control as stated in principle 2.
The internal audit function is established by management and the audit committee; principle 3 establishes structures, reporting lines, and authority.
Risk appetite is addressed in enterprise risk management, not in COSO principle 3 which covers governance structures and authority.
Financial reporting is an objective of internal control; principle 3 establishes structures and authority for governance oversight.
Profitability is a financial objective; principle 4 addresses the organization's commitment to attracting and retaining competent personnel.
Growth is a strategic objective; principle 4 focuses on demonstrating commitment to competence through policies and practices.
Market share is a competitive metric; principle 4 demonstrates commitment to competent personnel aligned with the control environment.
Principle 14 requires communication with all external parties, such as shareholders and regulators, not only regulators.
Principle 14 addresses external communication but also includes communicating ICFR information internally to relevant stakeholders.
Principle 14 includes communicating with external parties in addition to internal communication about internal control.
Testing control effectiveness is performed through attributes sampling, not variables sampling which estimates numerical values.
Identifying anomalies is a data analytics technique; variables sampling estimates population values such as dollar amounts or quantities.
Verifying system access is an access control test; variables sampling estimates numerical characteristics of populations.
Monetary values are estimated using variables sampling, not attributes sampling which tests for the presence or absence of a characteristic.
Physical quantities are determined through measurement or count; attributes sampling tests whether a specific attribute is present or absent.
Time measurements are numerical values assessed through variables sampling, not attributes sampling.
Internal audit should have access to all records, personnel, and properties across the organization, not only IT systems.
Internal audit requires access to management reports as well as all other records and personnel, not only management reports.
Internal audit needs access to all financial and non-financial records, personnel, and properties, not only financial records.
Communication methods include policies and training; pre-numbered documents are a control activity ensuring transaction completeness.
Monitoring includes ongoing evaluations and separate assessments; pre-numbered documents are a control activity for transaction recording.
Risk assessment identifies and analyzes risks; pre-numbered documents are a control activity that helps prevent omission or duplication.
Employee satisfaction is an HR concern; dual custody is a control that reduces theft risk by requiring two individuals.
Dual custody increases control costs because two people are required for access, not reduces them.
Dual custody may decrease operating efficiency due to coordination requirements; its purpose is reducing theft risk.
Compensating controls mitigate deficiencies in other controls; mandatory vacations are a detective control that can reveal fraud during the employee's absence.
Preventive controls stop fraud before it occurs; mandatory vacations detect fraud when another person performs the role temporarily.
Corrective controls remediate issues after detection; mandatory vacations detect fraudulent activity during the employee's absence.
Option A uses market share to evaluate profit centers. Market share is a marketing metric; profit centers are held accountable for profit relative to budgeted targets.
Option B relies on residual income only. While residual income is a useful metric, profit center evaluation primarily compares actual profit to budgeted profit.
Option D evaluates profit centers by ROI only. ROI is the primary metric for investment centers; profit center managers are evaluated on profit performance against budget.
Option B requires only segment revenue disclosure. ASC 280 also mandates disclosure of segment profit or loss and segment assets, not revenue alone.
Option C requires disclosure of segment liabilities only. ASC 280 specifies segment assets, not liabilities, as a required disclosure item.
Option D limits disclosure to segment profit. When segment assets are regularly reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, they must also be disclosed.

Option C states the segment does not meet the test. The asset test is met when segment assets are 10% or more of total combined assets, including exactly 10%.

Option C assigns report preparation to external auditors. Management accountants prepare internal performance reports; auditors review, not prepare, such reports.
Option D limits reporting to an annual cycle. Performance reports must be frequent enough to enable timely corrective action, not merely annual.
Option B assigns variance analysis to tax reporting. Tax reporting uses actual results to determine tax liability, not budget comparisons for internal management.

Option A treats the standard cost card as showing only budgeted cost. The card disaggregates each cost element into its standard price and standard quantity components.

Option D describes practical standards that include allowances for downtime and waste. Ideal standards assume no such inefficiencies exist.

Option C describes perfect conditions. Practical standards recognize real-world conditions including normal inefficiencies that ideal standards ignore.

Option B associates a negative variance with favorability. For revenue, a negative variance (actual below budget) is unfavorable, not favorable.
Option C describes an unfavorable revenue variance. Budgeted revenue exceeding actual means revenue fell short of expectations.
Option D describes a scenario with no variance. When actual equals budgeted revenue, there is no variance to classify as favorable or unfavorable.
Option A reduces budgeting to only historical data. The behavioral dimension addresses how budgets influence employee motivation, participation, and goal alignment.
Option B limits budgeting to cost calculation. The behavioral aspect encompasses how the budgeting process affects employee attitudes, effort, and organizational commitment.
Option D reduces behavioral budgeting to revenue projection. Behavioral aspects span the entire budgeting process, including participation, goal setting, and performance evaluation.
